title: Gender, number, animacy; the parts of a word

blocks.text: A division of nouns and pronouns (and sometimes of other parts of speech) into masculine or feminine, and sometimes other categories like neuter or common, and animate or inanimate.
Of, pertaining or belonging to the male grammatical gender, in languages that have gender distinctions.
Of, pertaining or belonging to the female grammatical gender, in languages that have gender distinctions.
Having a form which is not masculine nor feminine.
Of a word or phrase, the state of being singular, dual or plural, shown by inflection.
A form of a word that refers to only one person or thing.
A word in the form in which it potentially refers to something other than one person or thing.
The characteristic of a noun, dependent on its living or sentient nature, which affects grammatical features.
The last morpheme of a word, added to some base to make an inflected form (such as -s in "dogs").
The main part of an uninflected word to which affixes may be added to form inflections of the word.
The primary lexical unit of a word, which carries the most significant aspects of semantic content and cannot be reduced into smaller constituents.
A morpheme added to the beginning of a word to modify its meaning.
A morpheme added at the end of a word to modify the word's meaning.
Exercises: which term each definition is of. Review Terms, at the foot of the page, drills this module's terms.
